title: Ownership Lanes and Cutover Health API for Roadmap Dependencies
creator: Priya Patel
description: Problem statement: cross-team roadmap dependencies are currently tracked as free-text tickets and spreadsheets. During cutovers we lack machine-readable, queryable signals for ownership, accept criteria, and health leading to late escalations and misrouted rollbacks. This ticket proposes a lightweight API + taxonomy (Ownership Lanes) and a Cutover Health model to standardize signals across PM/Eng/Design/Security/Infra teams.
background: Over the last four quarters we've seen repeated incidents where a dependency was marked as 'ready' in a doc but failed during integration testing. Existing dependency artifacts are inconsistent: some teams use Linear comments, others use a Google Sheet or Confluence tables. The Console rollout and Dedicated capacity launches highlighted the operational cost of ambiguous handoffs. We need a canonical, queryable surface for readiness that can drive dashboards, alerts, and gating logic in release automation.
scope: Define Ownership Lanes taxonomy, implement a minimal Cutover Health score, expose a read/write API and Linear integration, create a Console widget for dependents, and run a pilot with Infra and Serving Runtime teams.
out_of_scope: Full automation of cross-team escalations, enforcement of contractual SLAs, and retrofitting legacy backlog items in other Qs.
acceptance_criteria: Ownership Lanes document published and reviewed by Eng/Design/Security/Infra
Cutover Health model (Healthy/At Risk/Blocked) implemented and exposed via API
API endpoints: GET /v1/dependencies/:key, POST /v1/dependencies (create/update) with validation
Linear integration creates/updates PM ticket when a dependency health flips to Blocked
Pilot run completed with two initiatives and dashboard shows health rollup per initiative
proposed_solution: 1) Create a simple taxonomy: lanes = {Owner, Implementer, Validator, Stakeholders} with required fields (owner, target-cutover, acceptance-criteria, test-status). 2) Implement Cutover Health: binary signals aggregated (integration-tests-passing, security-review-passed, infra-provisioned) mapped to Healthy/At Risk/Blocked. 3) Expose API with JSON payloads and a small SDK helper in the Console to read/write. 4) Build a lightweight Linear webhook adapter: on dependency create/update, attach canonical fields to the Linear ticket and keep ID mapping. 5) Pilot with Serving Runtime and Infra for one Dedicated and one Console rollout.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Finalize taxonomy and field set; stakeholder review session
Week 2: Implement API (read/write) and Linear webhook adapter; unit tests
Week 3: Console widget + rollout dashboard; onboard pilot teams
Week 4: Pilot monitoring, capture feedback, tweak model thresholds, prepare rollout notes
metrics: Mean time to detect (MTTD) a Blocked dependency during cutover < 2 hours
% of dependencies with complete Ownership Lanes metadata > 85% for pilot initiatives
Number of cross-team escalations avoided (qualitative post-pilot)
Time saved on coordination per cutover (baseline vs pilot)
risks: Teams may under-provide metadata, weakening signal quality
Overfitting health model thresholds causing false positives/negatives
Linear API rate limits or schema drift complicate synchronization
Security review cadence may delay pilot if SRE/SEC time is constrained
